history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas: the centre of Sati's eyebrows (symbolic of her mind) is believed to have fallen here; she is worshipped as Mahishamardini with Bhairava Vakranath, and the name is linked to sage Ashtavakra ('bakra' = bent), who is said to have performed penance here. The Oriya-style temple complex (Mahishamardini and Vakranath shrines) holds ancient paintings of the goddess preserved by the ASI. Famous for its natural hot springs (Agni, Surya, Brahma, Amrita, Dudh, Khar Kund etc., Agni Kund ~80–93°C, mineral-rich, reputed medicinal) on the banks of the Paphara/Bakreshwar river. A big Shivaratri mela draws huge crowds. Town note: CSV 'Birbhum' is the district — the temple town is Bakreshwar. Exact construction date/dynasty undocumented — flag.

name: Bakreshwar Temple
town_description: Bakreshwar is a pilgrim village on the southern bank of the Bakreshwar (Paphara) stream in Birbhum district, ~7 miles north-west of Dubrajpur and ~18 km south-west of Suri — called the 'village of deities' for its many temples, also noted for its thermal springs and the nearby Bakreshwar Thermal Power Station township.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~230 km)
travel.railway: Dubrajpur (~7 miles); Sainthia Junction also cited
travel.road: Metalled road Suri–Dubrajpur via Bakreshwar; direct buses from Suri, Dubrajpur, Bolpur, Sainthia and Durgapur

visitor_information.best_time: October–March (winter is ideal for hot-spring bathing)
